note: Every row is a claim the site makes. class: OFFICIAL (organizer or primary literature, read from the linked page), MEASURED (computed in this checkout from hash-verified bytes by a named script), BLOCKED (cannot be obtained in this environment, with the reason). Nothing here is asserted from memory.

sources.topic: Competition problem statement, metric, submission contract
sources.claim: Distance-weighted Tversky index with a 300 m triangular kernel, 100 m pixels, alpha 0.2 / beta 0.8; EPSG:32611, float32, values in [0,1], NaN outside the mapped area only; the public USGS fault database is incomplete and an expert panel labelled the new faults that form the test set; initial and final rounds with an expanded label set for the final.
Pixels corresponding to known USGS/INGENIOUS faults are masked out of evaluation and do not count towards the penalty terms; confirmed to apply to the final round as well.
Any fault pixel not already captured by USGS/INGENIOUS counts as new, and can include newly mapped geometry of an existing fault system.
Three scored submissions per rolling week; a single submission is selected for scoring across both rounds.
The feature stack, existing-fault raster and example submission used here come from the GeoDAWN / DOE GEMS data release.

Defines t(x) = grad m1 x grad m2, shows it vanishes where the two models change in the same direction, requires no petrophysical relationship between the properties, and measures shared structure rather than shared amplitude.

sources.topic: Cross-gradient applied to gravity and magnetics
sources.claim: Extends cross-gradient coupling to potential-field pairs; the reference the brief cites for gravity+magnetics.

sources.topic: Data-domain horizontal-gradient angle and cross product
sources.claim: The angle and cross product of the horizontal gradients of gravity and reduced-to-pole magnetics used directly in the data domain, without inversion. This is the construction implemented in src/gems49/crossgrad.py.

Free, public-domain U.S. Government elevation products; the named source for a higher-resolution elevation surface than the supplied detrended elevation. Obtainable in principle, but this environment gets HTTP 000 from the S3 endpoint and the region is terabytes at 1 m.
Programmatic lookup of 3DEP tile lists; documented and free, not reachable from this sandbox.
Free, public-domain seismicity for independent structural corroboration; not reachable from this sandbox (all non-GitHub/non-PyPI hosts return HTTP 000 through the available transport).

sources.topic: USGS Quaternary Fault and Fold Database
sources.claim: Public-domain mapped Quaternary faults, useful as context but explicitly not a label source: predicting these would be a relabel of what the scorer masks out.
Free DOE-hosted geothermal data and play-fairway studies for the Great Basin; used as context only.
Top public scores observed on 2026-10-06: 0.3774, 0.3345, 0.3262, 0.3222, 0.3220; the reference artifact studied from a sibling repository sits at 0.2778.

The submission page and leaderboard require an authenticated session; /data/ redirects unauthenticated requests to /accounts/login/ and the terms forbid automated monitoring, so no leaderboard score for the file released here is available. Every number on this site is a proxy computed from the public data.
